key_insight: World Tracing bridges the gap between faithful image alignment and complete 3D generation. It predicts geometry that stays attached to visible pixels while also extending beyond what the camera can see.
problem_solved: Existing image-to-3D methods usually face a trade-off: depth methods are accurate but only cover visible surfaces, while generative 3D models create complete shapes that can drift away from the input image. This paper addresses the need for both pixel-level alignment and full object/world completion.
method: Introduces a generative pixel-aligned geometry representation called World Tracing.
For each input pixel, predicts an ordered stack of camera-space 3D points rather than only a single depth value.
Uses the stacked geometry to represent both observed surfaces and hidden/occluded structure beyond the visible region.
impact: This approach can improve 3D reconstruction and generation tasks where both visual faithfulness and shape completeness matter. For practitioners, it offers a more reliable representation for converting images into 3D scenes or objects without losing alignment to the input.

paper_title: World Tracing: Generative Pixel-Aligned Geometry Beyond the Visible
